record.original_question: Which closed simply-connected 4-manifolds admit a 5-colored graph Γ in G_s^(4) and a cyclic permutation ε of the color set such that g_{ε0,ε2,ε4} = 1 and g_{ε1,ε3,ε4} = 1 and the associated T(Γ, ε) is a gem-induced trisection, so that the trisection genus equals the second Betti number β2(M)? More generally, can one characterize topologically the 4-manifolds that admit gems satisfying the hypotheses used in Proposition 26, or at least identify broad classes of manifolds that do so?

evidence.quote: Proposition 26 ([10]) gT(M) = β2(M) for each closed (simply-connected) 4-manifold M which admits a 5-colored graph Γ ∈ G^(4)_s representing M with gε0,ε2,ε4 = 1 and gε1,ε3,ε4 = 1 (ε being a cyclic permutation of ∆4), so that T(Γ, ε) is a gem-induced trisection.
It would be very interesting to characterize topologically 4-manifolds admitting gems which satisfy the hypotheses of the above statement, or at least to find classes satisfying them.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. A 5-colored graph is a pair (Γ, γ) where Γ is a multigraph that is regular of degree 5 and γ is an edge-coloring γ : E(Γ) → Δ_4 = {0,1,2,3,4} such that edges meeting at a common vertex carry pairwise distinct colors. Such a graph encodes a closed PL 4-manifold M(Γ) by the standard colored-graph (gem) construction: each vertex represents a 4-simplex and edges of color i identify the 3-faces opposite the i-th vertex of adjacent simplices. Let G_s^(4) denote the class of bipartite 5-colored graphs that represent closed simply-connected PL 4-manifolds.

For any subset S ⊂ Δ_4, write Γ_S for the subgraph spanned by edges whose colors lie in S, and let g_S denote the number of connected components of Γ_S. Given a cyclic permutation ε = (ε_0, ε_1, ε_2, ε_3, ε_4) of Δ_4, the colored-graph data determines a canonical decomposition T(Γ, ε) of M(Γ) into three 4-dimensional handlebodies whose pairwise and triple intersections form the strata of a (Gay–Kirby) trisection; when this decomposition is in fact a trisection it is called the gem-induced trisection associated with (Γ, ε).

The trisection genus gT(M) of a closed 4-manifold M is the minimum, over all trisections of M, of the genus of the central surface.

It is known that if Γ ∈ G_s^(4) represents M and there exists a cyclic permutation ε of Δ_4 such that
  g_{ε_0, ε_2, ε_4} = 1   and   g_{ε_1, ε_3, ε_4} = 1,
and such that T(Γ, ε) is a gem-induced trisection, then
  gT(M) = β_2(M),
where β_2(M) is the second Betti number of M.

Problem. Characterize topologically the closed simply-connected 4-manifolds M for which there exist a 5-colored graph Γ ∈ G_s^(4) representing M and a cyclic permutation ε of Δ_4 satisfying the two conditions g_{ε_0, ε_2, ε_4} = 1 and g_{ε_1, ε_3, ε_4} = 1 with T(Γ, ε) a gem-induced trisection. More generally, identify broad classes of closed (simply-connected) PL 4-manifolds that admit gems satisfying these hypotheses, and hence for which the trisection genus equals the second Betti number.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of topologically characterizing the 4-manifolds admitting gems that satisfy the hypotheses guaranteeing gT(M) = β_2(M) is posed as an open question in the gem/trisection literature. Recent works (e.g., on gem-induced trisections and on estimating trisection genus via gem theory, 2024–2025) confirm partial results — all standard simply-connected 4-manifolds satisfy the conclusion — but a full topological characterization has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Gem-induced trisections of compact PL 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces gem-induced trisections and shows that for a class of closed simply-connected 4-manifolds the (G-)trisection genus equals β_2.
status_evidence.claim: Result establishing gT(M)=β_2(M) under the colored-graph hypotheses; characterization left implicit.

status_evidence.title: Estimating trisection genus via gem theory
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work giving estimates and computational methods for trisection genus from gems, indicating the characterization problem remains a research topic.
status_evidence.claim: The topological characterization of manifolds admitting such gems is still being investigated.

status_evidence.title: Trisections of PL 4-Manifolds Arising from Colored Triangulations
status_evidence.snippet: Extends gem-induced trisections to broader settings; does not provide a full topological characterization of the hypothesis class.
